* Provides static methods for creating mutable {@code Set} instances easily and
 * other static methods for working with Sets.
 *

methods.name: public static HashSet<K> newHashSet()
methods.comment:
* Creates an empty {@code HashSet} instance. * *

Note: if {@code E} is an {@link Enum} type, use {@link * EnumSet#noneOf} instead. * *

Note: if you only need an immutable empty Set, * use {@link Collections#emptySet} instead. * * @return a newly-created, initially-empty {@code HashSet}

methods.name: public static HashSet<E> newHashSet(E... elements)
methods.comment:
* Creates a {@code HashSet} instance containing the given elements. * *

Note: due to a bug in javac 1.5.0_06, we cannot support the * following: * *

{@code Set set = Sets.newHashSet(sub1, sub2);} * *

where {@code sub1} and {@code sub2} are references to subtypes of {@code * Base}, not of {@code Base} itself. To get around this, you must use: * *

{@code Set set = Sets.newHashSet(sub1, sub2);} * * @param elements the elements that the set should contain * @return a newly-created {@code HashSet} containing those elements (minus * duplicates)

methods.name: public static SortedSet<E> newSortedSet()
methods.comment:
* Creates an empty {@code SortedSet} instance.
     *
     * @return a newly-created, initially-empty {@code SortedSet}.

methods.name: public static SortedSet<E> newSortedSet(E... elements)
methods.comment:
* Creates a {@code SortedSet} instance containing the given elements.
     *
     * @param elements the elements that the set should contain
     * @return a newly-created {@code SortedSet} containing those elements (minus
     *     duplicates)

methods.name: public static ArraySet<E> newArraySet(E... elements)
methods.comment: * Creates a {@code ArraySet} instance containing the given elements.
